video_title: Two-Phase Commit: Why We Vote Before We Commit
core_insight: Two-phase commit separates voting from decision so distributed resources can agree on all-or-nothing without a shared lock, trading availability for strong atomicity.

scenes.voice: Why do we need a two-phase commit? Because you need one logical transaction across databases that can't share a lock.
scenes.visual: Two separate database icons DB1 and DB2 with money moving between them, network line flickering.

scenes.voice: Debit A in DB1 and credit B in DB2. If the network drops after one write, money is created or destroyed. Distribution means no single writer, network is unreliable, participants can crash.
scenes.visual: Sequence of debit succeeds, credit fails, balance mismatch highlighted in red.

scenes.voice: Obvious fix is write both and hope. That's best effort, fast and cheap but inconsistent. The constraint is we need all-or-nothing with independent resources.
scenes.visual: Simple one-phase arrows to both DBs with a warning icon.

scenes.voice: Two-phase commit uses a coordinator like a wedding planner. Phase one Prepare: ask every participant can you hold it and will you definitely hold it if I say go? No one commits yet, just votes yes or no.
scenes.visual: Coordinator icon sending PREPARE to P1 and P2, participants locking resources.

scenes.voice: Phase two Commit or Abort. If all yes, coordinator tells everyone commit. If any no or timeout, abort. Participants must persist their vote to recover after crash.
scenes.visual: Mermaid sequence diagram showing Client, Coordinator, P1, P2 with PREPARE, YES/NO, then COMMIT/ABORT.
scenes.mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
participant Client
participant Coordinator
participant P1
participant P2
Client->>Coordinator: begin
Coordinator->>P1: PREPARE
Coordinator->>P2: PREPARE
P1-->>Coordinator: YES / NO
P2-->>Coordinator: YES / NO
alt all YES
Coordinator->>P1: COMMIT
Coordinator->>P2: COMMIT
else any NO
Coordinator->>P1: ABORT
Coordinator->>P2: ABORT
end

scenes.voice: This gives strong atomicity but trades availability and latency. A yes voter must stay locked until decision. Coordinator or participant unreachable means everyone blocks. No partition tolerance.
scenes.visual: Coordinator down icon, participants stuck with locks, clock showing wait.

scenes.voice: So use 2PC for small bounded critical transactions like financial settlement where intermediate inconsistency is not allowed. For large availability-sensitive systems prefer Saga with compensating actions.
scenes.visual: Decision diamond: small critical set → 2PC, large/available → Saga.

scenes.voice: Two-phase commit is vote first, decide later. You buy atomicity by accepting blocking and a coordinator as a reliability hotspot.
scenes.visual: Wedding planner metaphor with check marks, final takeaway text.

mental_model: Think of 2PC as a group reservation with a planner: first collect firm yes/no votes while holding resources, then broadcast a single commit or abort decision. Everyone moves together or not at all, and the planner is the critical point.
final_takeaway: 2PC buys distributed atomicity by separating voting from decision, at the cost of availability, latency, and a blocking coordinator.
